Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. EdgeCloud confirmed they want to move forward but need to increase the committed capacity on the order form from 8 to 16 GPUs and adjust pricing tiers for year 2. I attached the MSA and order form with our in-line redlines (highlighted) — mainly liability language in Section 9, a data retention clarification, and the capacity table on the order form.

Can you confirm Redwood can accept the capacity bump and advise on pricing impact? Procurement also asked for a clear timeline for legal review so they can align their renewal windows.

Samantha — thanks for sending these over and for the clear notes. Quick answers up front:
- Capacity: we can support the 16-GPU committed tier; Ben and I will run a fast pricing calc for the annual commitment vs pay-as-you-go.
- Legal redlines: looping in Rishi (GC) to review the MSA comments — he may propose alternative language rather than the exact redline in v3.
- Timeline: we should have legal comments back by EOD Wed (11/4) and a clean order form by Thu (11/5) if there are no major sticking points.

I'm attaching a one-page mutual action plan (MAP) to capture milestones so both teams are aligned. Ben — can you confirm the unit economics change and provide a quick delta to insert in the MAP? Rishi/Laura — please flag any high-risk MSA items.

Vanessa / Samantha — quick pricing note: bumping to 16 committed GPUs moves EdgeCloud from our standard S-8 tier to a custom S-16 discount band. Estimated impact: ~+32% ARR vs the existing 8-GPU commitment, but with better per-GPU effective rate in year 1 and an option to cap year-2 increases at CPI + 2%. I'll put numbers in the MAP (and a short table in the order form).

If procurement is sensitive to an upfront price change, we can offer a 60-day price protection clause for year 2 and staggered billing for the onboarding month.

Ben Carter
Account Director, West
Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 11:44:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial redlines + capacity ask (EdgeCloud)

Thanks — I reviewed the redline doc briefly. Top-level legal notes:
1) Section 9 (Limitation of Liability): EdgeCloud's proposed cap is higher than our standard; propose language that ties cap to fees paid in prior 12 months (we can accept but limited to 12 months' fees for material claims).
2) Data retention: we can accept more restrictive retention for regulated data but will need the customer to specify which datasets; recommend a limited-scope SOW addendum rather than changing the MSA.
3) Audit / SOC evidence: EdgeCloud asked for raw audit logs retention — we can provide summarized logs and an SOC 2 attestation; raw logs require a separate agreement and may be a chargeable service.

I'll add tracked-change suggestions to your doc and leave comments where we need commercial sign-off. If Ben prefers, we can accept a short form amendment to the MSA that references the Order Form and an attached SOW to capture retention + responsibilities.

Rishi Malhotra
General Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Samantha Young <samantha@edgecloud.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@edgecloud.com, EdgeCloud Legal <legal@edgecloud.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 08:36:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial redlines + capacity ask (EdgeCloud)

Rishi — thanks for the quick review. A few clarifications from our side:
- For liability cap we are comfortable with 12 months' fees if Redwood can confirm a carve-out for gross negligence and willful misconduct in the MSA language.
- Data retention: we'll enumerate the regulated datasets in the SOW addendum — happy to sign an SOW instead of changing the MSA.
- Audit logs: procurement needs the raw logs for their internal monitoring. If that's a separate paid add-on, can you provide an estimate so procurement can approve the delta?

Procurement also asked whether DocuSign flow can be started once legal agrees on redlines, and whether a signature matrix (who signs from each side) can be attached to the DocuSign envelope.

Best,
Samantha Young
